forward_guidance.text: The 10-Q gives no numeric revenue or EPS guidance. Qualitative and partial items: (1) FX is expected to have a favorable impact on full-year 2026 net operating revenues, operating income and operating cash flow, based on spot rates and hedging coverage. (2) The 2026 underlying effective tax rate is expected to be about 19.9% before significant items and excluding any adverse IRS litigation outcome. (3) 2026 capital expenditures are expected to be about 2.2 billion. (4) Full-year concentrate sales volume growth is expected to be slightly behind unit case volume growth. Q4 2026 has six fewer days than Q4 2025. (5) Share repurchases are expected to offset employee stock-based compensation dilution. (6) The sale of part of the Africa bottling interest to CCHBC is expected to close by end of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.
forward_guidance.source_citation: 10-Q, Item 2 MD&A: Net Operating Revenues; Operating Income; Income Taxes; Liquidity, Capital Resources and Financial Position; Concentrate Sales Volume; Note 2

key_risks.description: U.S. IRS transfer-pricing dispute (tax years 2007-2009). The 11th Circuit heard the appeal on June 25, 2026, and no decision is disclosed. If the Tax Court position is upheld, the 6.0 billion deposit plus 514 million of accrued interest receivable would not be refunded. Potential incremental tax and interest for 2010-2025 is about 14 billion as of Dec 31, 2025, and continued application of the Tax Court methodology would add about 3.8 points to the 2026 effective tax rate. The Company recorded a 529 million reserve and believes it is more likely than not to prevail.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q, Note 9 Commitments and Contingencies - Tax Audits; Part II Item 1 Legal Proceedings

key_risks.description: fairlife ransomware event disclosed in an 8-K on July 16, 2026. It caused a temporary suspension of production, and a majority of production has resumed. The Company currently believes the incident is not reasonably likely to have a material impact, but the investigation is ongoing.

BodyArmor trademark impairment risk. The remaining carrying value is 2,440 million and fair value approximates carrying value at July 3, 2026. A shortfall versus revised projections or a higher discount rate would likely trigger a further impairment.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q, Item 2 MD&A, Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates

key_risks.description: Higher commodity costs and increased marketing spend are pressuring segment margins (North America, Asia Pacific, EMEA). Advertising expense rose to 1,565 million from 1,328 million in the quarter.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q, Item 2 MD&A, Gross Profit Margin; Selling, General and Administrative Expenses; Operating Income

key_risks.description: FX volatility. Q2 operating income benefited 5% from FX, and a reversal of weaker U.S. dollar trends would reduce that tailwind. The stronger dollar versus the yen, rupee, lira and peso is already a headwind in some segments.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q, Item 2 MD&A, Foreign Exchange; Operating Income

key_risks.description: Africa bottling divestiture execution risk. Closing requires regulatory approvals, with the sale expected by end of 2026. The held-for-sale assets (5,438 million) carry a 1,207 million allowance, and the Q2 net gain came from revised estimates.
Asia Pacific price/mix of -9% in Q2 (affordability initiatives and mix) is diluting revenue growth despite strong volume.
Baltimore plastic-packaging litigation. The remaining public nuisance claim was dismissed by the Baltimore Circuit Court on July 23, 2026. The 10-Q does not state whether an appeal has been filed.
key_risks.source_citation: 10-Q, Part II Item 1 Legal Proceedings, Environmental Matter

bull_case: Q2 2026 revenue +7%, operating income +9% and operating margin up 80bps to 34.9%, with growth across volume, price/mix and FX.
Worldwide unit case volume +5% and concentrate sales +4%, with growth in all four geographic segments and strong Asia Pacific (+8% unit cases).
Management expects FX to remain a tailwind to full-year revenue, operating income and operating cash flow.
Six-month operating cash flow was 7.5 billion, with 16.4 billion of cash and investments and 6.6 billion of unused backup credit lines. Interest expense fell 17% on lower short-term debt.

The 8th Circuit's 3M ruling is described as highly supportive of the Company's position in the 11th Circuit IRS appeal, argued June 25, 2026. A favorable outcome could return the 6.0 billion deposit plus interest.
Corporate costs are falling (operating loss 256 vs 329), and the dividend was raised to 0.53 per quarter from 0.51.
bear_case: Part of the Q2 EPS beat versus last year came from non-operating items: a 320 million net gain on securities and a 66 million Africa impairment reduction, which may not recur.
About 5 points of the 9% operating income growth came from FX, which could fade if the U.S. dollar strengthens.
Asia Pacific price/mix was -9%, and EMEA operating income declined despite revenue growth due to higher marketing and operating expenses.
Commodity costs are higher and marketing spend is up sharply (advertising +18% in Q2), pressuring North America and other segments.
The IRS dispute carries a potential approximately 14 billion incremental liability (plus a 6.0 billion deposit at risk), and would add about 3.8 points to the effective tax rate if lost.
The fairlife ransomware outage and BodyArmor's near-impairment fair value add idiosyncratic downside in North America.
Q4 2026 has six fewer days, and concentrate volume is expected to lag unit case volume for the full year. Six-month volume was also helped by six extra days in Q1.

what_to_watch.text: Q3 2026 results versus Q2 trends: concentrate sales volume vs unit case volume (Q3 should not be distorted by day-count), price/mix (especially Asia Pacific) and the size of the FX tailwind.
Any update on the fairlife ransomware recovery, including full production resumption, lost sales or remediation costs in North America.
Eleventh Circuit decision in the IRS transfer-pricing case, argued June 25, 2026, and any change to the 529 million reserve or the effective tax rate guide (about 19.9% ex-significant items).
Commodity cost and marketing spend trends and their effect on gross margin (62.9% in Q2) and segment operating margins.
BodyArmor performance versus revised projections, given fair value approximates the 2,440 million carrying value.
Africa bottling sale to CCHBC: progress on regulatory approvals and closing by year-end 2026, and any further held-for-sale adjustments.

Cash flow comparisons: Q2 2026 included the full Q2 dividend payment, whereas substantially all of the 2025 Q2 dividend was paid in Q3, which will affect Q3 year-over-year financing cash flow. The next dividend of 0.53 is payable Oct 1, 2026.
